title: Mantra, Stotra, Aarti and Bhajan Library
intro: Devotional texts with their source and their verification status. Items marked 'not included' are absent deliberately — they are either copyright-restricted or could not be sourced from a verifiable edition, and neither is a reason to transcribe from memory.
editorialNote: Editorial content authored for this app. It has not been through independent scholarly review. See the Content Verification page.

items.title: Navarna Mantra (Navakshari)
items.deva: ॐ ऐं ह्रीं क्लीं चामुण्डायै विच्चे
items.iast: oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ klīṃ cāmuṇḍāyai vicce
items.attribution: Shakta tantric tradition; the seed mantra of Chandika, central to Saptashati recitation.
items.meaning: The nine-syllable mantra of Chandika. The first three syllables are bīja (seed) syllables and are not lexical words, so they are not translated word by word; cāmuṇḍāyai is 'to Chamunda' in the dative, and vicce is a bīja-like termination with no ordinary lexical meaning.
wordMeaning: bīja of the Goddess as maya
bīja of desire and of Kama
bīja-like termination; not a lexical word
items.pronunciation: om AIM hreem kleem cha-mun-DAI-yay vich-cheh

items.title: Namash Chandikayai
items.attribution: Devi Mahatmya; recited at the head of the text and before each chapter.
items.meaning: Salutation to Chandika. It appears in our imported source at the head of the kavacham, the argala, the kilaka and chapter 1.
items.sourceRef: Appears verbatim in the imported durga700 source.

items.title: Ya Devi Sarvabhuteshu
items.attribution: Devi Mahatmya, chapter 5. Recited as the Devi Sukta during the path.
items.meaning: The Goddess addressed as present in all beings under twenty-one aspects — as Vishnu-maya, consciousness, intellect, sleep, hunger, shadow, power, thirst, forgiveness, kind, modesty, peace, faith, radiance, delight, mother, and error. Each verse is followed by the refrain 'namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ'.

items.title: Devi Kavacham
items.attribution: Durga Saptashati auxiliary recitation; 60 verses in our imported edition.
items.meaning: The 'armour' hymn. It assigns the nine forms to the limbs (nyasa), names the protecting goddesses of the directions, and is recited first in the Navangam order.

items.title: Argala Stotram
items.attribution: Durga Saptashati auxiliary recitation; 27 verses in our imported edition.
items.meaning: The 'bolt' hymn: a series of petitions ('give form, give victory, give fame, destroy my enemies') framed by Jaya tvam Devi Chamunde.

items.title: Kilaka Stotram
items.attribution: Durga Saptashati auxiliary recitation; 16 verses in our imported edition.
items.meaning: The 'pin' hymn, recited to remove obstacles to the recitation itself.

items.title: Devi Suktam (Rig Veda 10.125)
items.attribution: Rig Veda 10.125, the Vak Sukta; recited in the Devi path.
items.meaning: The seer Vak declares herself as the one who moves with the Rudras, the Vasus and the Adityas; who bears Soma, Pushan and Bhaga; who is queen, gatherer of wealth, and first among those worthy of sacrifice.

items.title: Aparadha Kshamapana Stotram
items.attribution: Durga Saptashati auxiliary recitation; 9 verses in our imported edition.
items.meaning: The closing prayer asking forgiveness for errors of pronunciation, memory and attention in the recitation. Notably it asks that whatever was mis-syllabled be made whole by the Goddess's grace rather than by the reciter's skill.

items.title: Chandika Dhyana
items.attribution: Placed at the head of the text in our imported edition; two dhyana blocks.
items.meaning: Meditation verses describing the form of Chandika, followed by the alternative (athava) dhyana that summarises the whole text in one verse: she who destroyed Madhu and Kaitabha, who uprooted Mahisha, who churned Dhumralochana, who consumed Raktabija, who destroyed Shumbha and Nishumbha, and who is the giver of siddhis.

items.title: Mahishasura Mardini Stotram
items.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Bana Bhatta; the attribution is traditional rather than established.
items.meaning: A twelve-verse hymn in a fast, percussive metre addressed to the slayer of Mahishasura.
items.textStatusNote: The full text is not reproduced here. It was not available from a source this build could verify, and it will not be transcribed from memory. Add it through the documented import process with a citable edition.

items.title: Durga Chalisa
items.attribution: Hindi devotional composition in the chalisa form; modern printed editions are commonly associated with Gita Press and similar publishers.
items.meaning: A forty-verse Hindi devotional hymn to Durga.
items.textStatusNote: Not reproduced. Recent printed editions are under copyright, and the app will not reproduce a copyrighted devotional text without permission. Licence it, then add it through the import process.
